## Summary

I added a Prefab `Book` aggregate to the app.

**`src/main/java/com/example/catalog/Book.java`** — the domain type, in package `com.example.catalog`:
- `@Aggregate` with `@Id Reference<Book> id` and `@Version long version`.
- Fields: `title` (`@NotBlank @Size(max = 200)`), `author` (`@NotBlank`), `isbn` (`@NotBlank`), and `publicationYear` (an `int`).
- `@Create` constructor for `POST /books`, plus `@GetById` for `GET /books/{id}`. Validation lives on the constructor parameters, as Prefab requires.

Prefab generated (under `target/`, not hand-written): `BookController`, `BookService`, `CreateBookRequest`/`BookResponse`, the repository, the `book` table migration, and a `BookClient` test helper.

**`src/test/java/com/example/catalog/BookIntegrationTest.java`** — an `@IntegrationTest` using the generated `BookClient`, verifying that a created book can be retrieved by id with all five fields intact, and that an unknown id returns 404.

Verified behavior, confirmed against the generated controller:
- `POST /books` → `201 Created` with a `Location` header ending in `/books/{id}` (the client's `createBook` asserts `isCreated()` and reads the id from `Location`).
- `GET /books/{id}` → the book JSON with `id`, `title`, `author`, `isbn`, `publicationYear`, or `404` when absent.
- Storage is PostgreSQL (`prefab-postgres` on the classpath; Prefab generates the `book` table migration).

`mvn -DskipTests compile`, `mvn -Dtest=BookIntegrationTest test`, and `mvn verify` all succeed (2 tests, 0 failures). The trailing `IOException` about `surefire-stijnvanbael` in the log is a sandbox temp-directory cleanup quirk at JVM shutdown — the build itself reports `BUILD SUCCESS`.

Done. The `Task` aggregate is implemented as a nested resource of `Project`, and the full build passes.

## What I added

**`src/main/java/com/example/planning/Task.java`** — a Prefab aggregate:
- `@Parent @NotNull Reference<Project> project` makes it a sub-resource, so the project id travels in the path (`/projects/{projectId}/...`).
- `@NotBlank String title` (required) and `boolean done`.
- `@Create Task(project, title)` sets `done = false` at creation.
- `@Update(path = "/complete", method = "POST") Task complete()` returns the new state with `done = true`.
- `@GetById` + `@GetList` give the by-id and paged endpoints.

**`src/test/java/com/example/planning/TaskIntegrationTest.java`** — a `@IntegrationTest` using the generated `ProjectClient`/`TaskClient`, covering create (201, not done), blank-title rejection, per-project listing, and complete (done=true).

## Verification

Prefab generated exactly the four required endpoints (confirmed in `target/prefab/agent-context.md` and the generated `TaskController`):
- `POST /projects/{projectId}/tasks` → `201 Created`, `Location: /projects/{projectId}/tasks/{id}`, body `{"title": ...}` (the `@Parent` id comes from the path, not the body).
- `GET /projects/{projectId}/tasks/{id}` → `TaskResponse` exposing `id`, `title`, `done` (plus `version`/`project`).
- `GET /projects/{projectId}/tasks` → Spring Data `PagedModel` whose `content` array holds that project's tasks only.
- `POST /projects/{projectId}/tasks/{id}/complete` → `200 OK`.

`mvn verify` → **BUILD SUCCESS**, `TaskIntegrationTest` 4/4 passing. No hand-written controllers, entities, migrations, or DTOs — everything came from the annotated record.

One implementation note worth flagging: `Project`'s id is itself a `Reference<Project>`, so the create constructor passes `project.id()` directly rather than wrapping it in `new Reference<>(...)` — the obvious `new Reference<>(project.id())` form doesn't compile.

Done. The validation is in place and the full build passes.

## What I changed

**`src/main/java/com/example/crm/Customer.java`** — added Jakarta validation to the `@Create` constructor parameters (Prefab requires validation on the constructor parameters, not the record components; these propagate onto the generated `CreateCustomerRequest`):

```java
@Create
public Customer(@NotBlank @Size(max = 100) String name, @NotBlank @Email String email) {
    this(Reference.create(), 0L, name, email);
}
```

This makes `POST /customers` reject invalid input with `400 Bad Request` before anything is persisted:
- `name` — `@NotBlank` (required, not blank) + `@Size(max = 100)` (at most 100 chars)
- `email` — `@NotBlank` (required) + `@Email` (valid e-mail address)

Valid requests are unaffected — the request still binds and creates the customer with `201 Created`.

**`src/test/java/com/example/crm/CustomerIntegrationTest.java`** (new) — a `@IntegrationTest` using the generated `CustomerClient`, covering:
- valid `name`/`email` → created and retrievable (`201`)
- blank name → `400`
- missing (`null`) name → `400`
- name of 101 chars → `400`
- missing email → `400`
- invalid email (`"not-an-email"`) → `400`

## Verification
- `mvn -DskipTests compile` — clean (model and generated code compile).
- `mvn -Dtest=CustomerIntegrationTest test` — 6/6 pass.
- `mvn verify` — **BUILD SUCCESS**, all tests green. (The `ForkStarter IOException` lines in the log are a benign sandbox temp-directory artifact; the build reports success regardless.)

The change is minimal and idiomatic to Prefab — no hand-written controllers, DTOs, or migrations. No `prefab-security` or `@Event` types exist in this project, so no extra conformance test classes are generated; my integration test is the only test class, and it passes.
